assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks combine the magic-wavelength lattice idea with narrow optical transitions in neutral atoms, giving fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and below. This is a decisive measurement advance: it opens relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and dark-matter searches, and prepares a redefinition of the second. It fits my view that progress is limited by how precisely we can measure.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and led early Sr realizations in Tokyo. Jun Ye's group at JILA pushed performance to record stability and accuracy and developed the many-body clock work. This is a clean two-person configuration; the idea-versus-implementation split and the role of other Sr and Yb groups is a minor allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Many independent labs operate lattice clocks, intercomparisons agree at the 1e-18 level, and the technique is mature. Recognition is timely given the discussion of redefining the second.
uncertainties: The committee might see this as an extension of the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 Wineland-Haroche prize
Exact priority of the lattice-clock proposal relative to related proposals is from memory and not verified here

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms gives inertial sensors of extreme sensitivity: gravimeters, gradiometers, equivalence-principle tests and fine-structure-constant measurements. It created a new class of instrument and is moving toward field use in geodesy, navigation and resource exploration, which I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard developed early atom interferometry with gratings and the precision platform; Mlynek's group realized early atom-optics interferometry with nanofabricated structures; Kasevich built the light-pulse gravimeter and gradiometer. Others (for example Chu, Borde, Helmcke) also made foundational contributions, so a three-name set is a judgement call and may be contested.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many groups and partly commercialized, but the largest fundamental-physics payoffs (long-baseline tests, gravitational-wave detection) are still developing. Timely, but credit is complicated.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims complicate the laureate set
Parts of the underlying atom-optics toolkit may be seen as already covered by earlier cooling and trapping prizes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller 1995 proposal for trapped-ion quantum gates, followed by experimental demonstrations of controlled gates, entanglement and small algorithms with ions, established a concrete path to quantum information processing. The work set the standard for coherence control, gate fidelity and readout, which are the quantities I care about.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the theoretical proposal; Blatt led some of the most complete ion-trap quantum information experiments (teleportation, multi-ion entanglement, quantum simulation). Wineland's group, honored in 2012, did the first gate demonstration, which makes experimental credit sharing delicate. Bloch is a defensible fourth name for neutral-atom simulation, but I keep the trio focused on ion-based processing.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by multiple groups and now a commercial platform. The theory-plus-experiment pairing is mature, though overlap with the 2012 prize and the ongoing quantum-computing race leaves the timing question open.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 Wineland and Haroche prize
Whether the committee would rather reward neutral-atom simulation (Bloch) in the same package

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED showed strong coherent coupling of a superconducting qubit to a microwave resonator, giving dispersive readout, gates and the architecture used in most superconducting quantum processors. It is a major experimental and conceptual platform for quantum information, with coherence and readout fidelity improving by orders of magnitude.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf and collaborators published the 2004 proposal and demonstrated strong coupling in the same year. Others such as Girvin and Devoret are significant contributors, and Devoret was recognized in 2025 (from memory), so the credit boundary with that prize and with unlisted contributors is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is extensive and the architecture is industrially adopted. A recent prize on superconducting circuits may make the committee cautious about a second award in the same area so soon.
uncertainties: Proximity to the recent superconducting-circuit prize and possible overlap of laureates
Some key contributors are not among the supplied credited names, so the allocation may be incomplete

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond turned a point defect into a room-temperature quantum sensor of magnetic and electric fields, temperature and strain with nanoscale resolution. This is a measurement-method breakthrough that has spread into biology, materials science and geophysics, and fits my interest in sensing with uses beyond physics.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko's work first demonstrated optical detection and coherent control of single NV spins; Lukin's group contributed key quantum-sensing concepts and experiments. The supplied credit supports a two- or three-person prize; I omit Lukin from this configuration, but the choice is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Many groups reproduce and extend the technique; applications are maturing but commercial and clinical-level sensing impact is still emerging. Recognition is reasonably timely.
uncertainties: Whether Lukin should be included for sensing and many-body NV experiments
Priority among early NV pioneers is not settled by the supplied data

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spherical-aberration correctors for electron lenses overcame a limit that had stood since Scherzer's theorem and brought routine sub-angstrom imaging of atoms in materials. This instrument-level advance is fundamental for measuring structure and has transformed materials physics and nanoscience.
assessment.attribution: Rose provided the corrector theory, Haider and collaborators built the first working corrector in transmission microscopy, and Urban led the application to materials. This is a well-matched three-person division of theory, instrument and application, though others also contributed to scanning-microscope correctors.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated in commercial microscopes with clear community consensus. The development is mature, with some risk that it is regarded as engineering rather than physics.
uncertainties: Whether the committee treats it as physics or as instrumentation engineering
Contributions of others on scanning-microscope correctors are not in the supplied credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model and demanded extraordinary detector and analysis performance. It is among the clearest discoveries in modern physics, and precision coupling measurements continue to support the interpretation.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize went to the theory. The experiments involve thousands of people and the three-person limit is a serious problem. Gianotti was ATLAS spokesperson at the discovery, Jenni was a founding leader of ATLAS, and Virdee was a founder and leader of CMS. Della Negra is a strong alternative, so the choice among four is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by two experiments and more than a decade of data. Recognition would be timely, but the allocation problem is acute and arguably unresolved.
uncertainties: Allocation across ATLAS and CMS leadership is contested and needs judgement beyond the supplied data
Collaboration size makes individual credit hard to assess

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light for quantum-enhanced interferometry, proposed by Caves and implemented in GEO600 and LIGO, beats the shot-noise limit in detectors. It is a clear example of quantum measurement improving a major instrument, tied directly to gravitational-wave sensitivity.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the central theoretical proposal; Schnabel's group developed and demonstrated squeezed-light sources for GEO600 and related work; Mavalvala contributed to squeezing and quantum-noise work in LIGO. Kimble and other early squeezing experimenters also matter, which leaves allocation open.
assessment.maturity: Operating in gravitational-wave detectors with demonstrated gains, so confirmed. The 2017 prize covers gravitational-wave detection itself, and squeezing is a refinement of that platform, which may limit its priority.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2017 gravitational-wave prize and with squeezing credit given to others
Pioneers of the first squeezing experiments are not all among the supplied names
